keyVerseText: But with thee will I establish my covenant; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons' wives with thee.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew word בְּרִית (bᵉrîyth) is etymologically connected to the root בָּרָה (bârâh), which involves the idea of cutting or choosing. This suggests that a בְּרִית originally referred to a compact or covenant established through a ritual act of cutting, symbolizing a binding agreement made by passing between pieces of flesh. This literal sense of cutting adds a tangible, solemn dimension to the concept of covenant beyond the English term, emphasizing the seriousness and binding nature of the commitment.
usageInScripture: The word בְּרִית occurs 284 times in Scripture and is most frequently translated as 'of the covenant' or simply 'a covenant,' underscoring its central role in biblical theology. It is used to describe various forms of agreements, including alliances between men, constitutions under monarchs, and, most importantly, divine covenants between God and humanity. The range of translations such as 'my covenant,' 'his covenant,' and 'a league' highlights the word's flexibility in expressing both personal and communal, human and divine commitments.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding בְּרִית as a covenant rooted in a solemn, binding act of cutting enriches our grasp of God's promises and relationships with His people. It reveals that God's covenants are not casual or symbolic but are deeply serious, involving divine ordinances with tangible signs and pledges. This word frames the biblical narrative around God's faithful commitment to His people, anticipating the ultimate covenant fulfilled in Christ. For the Christian faith, it affirms that God's promises are sure, established through a divine pledge that invites trust and obedience.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 6:18 states, 'But with thee will I establish my covenant; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons' wives with thee.' Here, בְּרִית conveys God's solemn promise to Noah, a binding divine agreement that guarantees preservation amid judgment. The word emphasizes the seriousness and permanence of God's pledge, assuring Noah and his family of salvation through the ark. This use of בְּרִית highlights the covenant as a foundation of divine faithfulness and protection.
